body: Quantum Redshift is Curly Monsters' futuristic Xbox racing game, released in North America on 17 September 2002. Armed hovercraft race across eight courses, with each driver connected to a particular rival. The player steers a SPARC through the circuit while collecting energy for weapons and protection. Winning means managing the road and the other vehicles at the same time. Alternate routes create choices within the courses, while the tournament's increasing difficulty also increases speed, making a familiar stretch of track demand a more immediate response.

Colour-coded pickups charge the craft's offensive weapons and shields. Homing and direct-fire attacks provide different ways to interfere with a rival, but staying on the racing line remains essential. Points earned through victories, pickups and defeated opponents can improve the craft between events. Each tournament eventually leads to a Nemesis Challenge against the selected character's rival. The player therefore develops both a vehicle and a relationship with a particular opponent, returning to the track with stronger equipment and a clearer reason to watch one competitor's position.

Curly Monsters included former Psygnosis staff who had worked on Wipeout, including designer Nick Burcombe. Microsoft supported the production with a soundtrack commissioned from Junkie XL and character work involving Satoshi Ueda. Local multiplayer allowed up to four people to race together, while Time Attack let the player pursue a recorded ghost. The game received mixed reviews and did not sell enough to support the planned sequel. Its lasting identity comes from the combination of increasingly fast racing, driver rivalries and a soundtrack written specifically for those high-speed encounters.
